messages.subject: question on mplusObject
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

a short question from a newbie:
I am having trouble specifing

a) categorical variables
(e.g.
categorical="all;",
)

b) weights
(e.g.
weight="weight1;",
)

in mplusObject ().

Is there any way to specificy these settings through MplusAutomation?

Thank you for your help.
Thomas

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] question on mplusObject
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Those options both occur in the VARIABLE section in Mplus, so for example:

m <- mplusObject(
  TITLE = "Categorical Example;",
  VARIABLE = "CATEGORICAL = cyl;",
  MODEL = "cyl ON mpg;",
  usevariables=c("cyl", "mpg"),
  rdata = mtcars)

res <- mplusModeler(m,"tmp.dat", "tmp.inp", 1L)

You would specify weights similarly.  Be sure to include the weights variable in the usevariables option, because that tells R to include that variable in the dataset for Mplus (this is slightly different from Mplus' usevariables, which only refers to the variables in the model section, NOT that are used for clustering or weights (which I think is a bit silly).

Cheers,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] question on mplusObject
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Every command that would go in a particular Mplus section, you put into a single character string in R.  For example:

require(MplusAutomation)

m <- mplusObject(
  TITLE = "Categorical Example;",
  VARIABLE = "
    CATEGORICAL = cyl;

    WEIGHT=wt;
    USEVARIABLES = cyl mpg;",

  MODEL = "cyl ON mpg;",
  usevariables=c("cyl", "mpg","wt"),
  rdata = mtcars)

categorical, weight, usevariables, all belong to the VARIABLE section in Mplus, so you put them all together in one in R.  The reference for this is Chapters 15 & 16 from the Mplus manual (http://www.statmodel.com/download/usersguide/Mplus%20user%20guide%20Ver_7_r6_web.pdf), which is the best/most comprehensive lsit of sections in Mplus, and the various subcommands that go in them that I know.  That is what I patterned the sections in mplusObject from.

res <- mplusModeler(m,"tmp.dat", "tmp.inp", 1L)

res$results$parameters$unstandardized
  paramHeader param     est     se est_se  pval
1      CYL.ON   MPG  -0.944  0.631 -1.496 0.135
2  Thresholds CYL$1 -20.046 13.474 -1.488 0.137
3  Thresholds CYL$2 -17.347 11.704 -1.482 0.138
